tool.title: Check declared credential needs against workflow use and expiry, by name
tool.description: Compare each repository's declared credential needs (`credentials/needs.json`, profile and registry) with the `secrets.NAME` expressions its workflows reference (GitHub Actions' dollar-and-double-brace form, said in words because this text is rendered on a Jekyll page), with the secret names GitHub lists when a token allows it, and with any recorded expiry. NAMES ONLY — no value is ever read. Findings: used-not-declared, declared-not-used, declared-not-present, present-not-declared (reported, never deleted), naming advisories, and expiry (≤30 days minor, ≤7 major, expired critical). Exits 2 when anything could not be determined, which outranks clean; else 1 on a major or critical finding; else 0.

inputs.name: repos
inputs.description: Repository checkouts to check. Default: every repository the index mounts.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: Print the result as JSON instead of the human report.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: The exit status: 0 clean, 1 a major or critical finding, 2 could not determine.

selection.when: Before relying on a workflow's credentials, or to see which secrets a repository needs, uses and lacks.
selection.limits: Presence on GitHub is judged only when a token may list secret names (`list-secret-names`); without one that half is could-not-determine, never clean.
selection.cost: Reads workflow and declaration files; one API call per repository when a token is present.

$comment.comment:
Bean `jzba` (credentials proposal §6.2): the MCP and CLI parity of axis
6 — this node is what `src/mcp/project.ts` projects onto MCP, so the CLI
and the MCP tool are one declaration with one argv.
